Class Handler

java.lang.Object
java.net.URLStreamHandler
io.micronaut.runner.protocol.jar.Handler
public final class Handler extends URLStreamHandler
The jar: protocol handler of a runner application.

The class name and the package are dictated by the JDK: URL.getURLStreamHandler builds the name <package>.<protocol>.Handler for every package listed in java.protocol.handler.pkgs, loads it with the system class loader and instantiates it reflectively, so this class must stay public, must keep this name, and must keep a public no-argument constructor. The JDK's instance and the instance Handlers keeps for building URLs are different objects; both read the same static registration, so it makes no difference which one parses a URL.

What it parses

parseURL(URL, String, int, int) follows the JDK's jar handler exactly, because every library that ever built a jar URL by hand relies on those rules: the last "!/" separates the jar from the entry, so the nested form jar:file:/app.jar!/lib/dep.jar!/a/B.class names the entry a/B.class; a relative spec resolves against the entry of the context URL; and . and .. segments are folded inside the entry. It differs from the JDK in two deliberate ways: a .. that would climb out of the archive is rejected rather than silently clamped, and the inner URL is validated by its scheme instead of by constructing a URL, which keeps URL creation off the class loading path.

What it opens

Installing a handler for jar: is process wide, so this class sees every jar URL in the JVM, including the ones the JDK itself opens. A URL whose jar part is the registered archive is served by RunnerJarURLConnection; everything else, jar:file: of another file and jar:http: alike, is handed back to the JDK's own handler through Handlers.openDelegate(URL) and behaves exactly as it did before the launcher started.

1.0

    • parseURL

      protected void parseURL(URL url, String spec, int start, int limit)
      Parses a jar URL, following the JDK's jar handler.

      parseURL cannot declare a checked exception, so a malformed spec is rejected with an IllegalArgumentException, which URL turns into a MalformedURLException for the caller.

      Overrides:
      parseURL in class URLStreamHandler
      Parameters:
      url - the URL being built, whose fields this method sets
      spec - the whole specification being parsed
      start - the first character after jar:
      limit - the end of the specification, before any # reference

    • sameFile

      protected boolean sameFile(URL first, URL second)
      Compares two jar URLs by their text.

      The JDK compares the inner URLs as URLs, which builds two URL objects and, for a remote inner URL, resolves host names. Two URLs this launcher produced for the same entry are always spelled the same way, so comparing the text answers the same question without either cost. The consequence, which is why this is documented rather than hidden, is that two differently spelled URLs of the same entry are not equals here even though the JDK would say they are.

      Overrides:
      sameFile in class URLStreamHandler
      Parameters:
      first - the first URL
      second - the second URL
      Returns:
      whether both name the same jar and the same entry
